object.name: evi_tremolo
object.digest: Basic Tremolo effect with saturation and choice of LFO shapes
object.description: An example of a tremolo using evieve primitives. Variable control of LFOs for interesting modulation. The tremolo amplitude can be driven well above unity gain into an antialiased saturation stage.

inlets.name: reset
inlets.digest: Reset of internal LFO phases is naive and not antialiased.

outlets.name: hz
outlets.digest: The currently computed speed in Hz of the modulating LFOs. This is important for downstream processing because if @lfomode is on, this will not necessarily be synchronised with changes to the @rate attribute.

outlets.name: lfo
outlets.digest: Left LFO output for downstream synchronisation.

outlets.name: lfo
outlets.digest: Right LFO output for downstream synchronisation.

attributes.name: crossover
attributes.description: Crossover frequency in Hz. Below this crossover point (the bass) the audio is mono summed, saturated and added back into the wet output mix. Above this crossover point the audio is chanelled through the tremolo effect.

attributes.name: depth
attributes.description: Internally, increasing depth increases the amplitude size of the LFO movement.

attributes.name: drive
attributes.description: 0..1 equates to about 0..+10 dB drive gain into the saturation stage. evi.tremolo~ can be safely overdriven to modulation well above unity gain and remain antialiased on output.

attributes.name: lfoinvert
attributes.description: Invert the wave shape of the current LFO shape. Switching is synchronised to the zero phase of the LFOs.

attributes.name: lfomode
attributes.description: If on, changes to the speed (@rate) of the internal LFOs are synchronised to zero reset of phase, which can produce seemless updating of speed changes. Otherwise the speed (@rate) updates smoothly morphing changes.

attributes.name: lfoout
attributes.description: Switch the LFO outputs (outlets 3 and 4) to output raw 0..1 range or output the actual amplitude used by the effect.

attributes.name: lfowave
attributes.description: The shape of the LFOs driving the modulation. 0=bypass, 1=up, 2=down, 3=tri, 4=sine (default), 5=tanh, 6=square, 7=rand step, 8=rand linear, 9=rand cubic, 10=noise. Switching LFO wave is synchronised to zero crossing phase. LFOs are always slightly smoothed, even hard edges such as square and random.

attributes.name: lfowidth
attributes.description: The pulse width of the LFO wave shapes that use it: 3=triangle, 5=tanh, 6=square.

attributes.name: maxhz
attributes.description: The maximum in Hz that the @rate attribute can reach.

attributes.name: rate
attributes.description: The global speed of the LFO phases. This sets the speed (between 0..@maxhz) the LFOs scale the amplitudes (set by @depth and @drive).

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: The smoothing time of the internal parameters.

attributes.name: spread
attributes.description: The left/right spread of the audio outputs, actually the phase offset of the two internal LFOs. 0..1 is mapped to 0..180 degrees shift.
